blocs.texte: Pour demander la permission de faire quelque chose, on utilise des modaux polis comme 'May', 'Could' ou 'Can', suivis du sujet et de la base verbale.

May I + base verbale ? (le plus formel et poli). Exemple : May I leave the table? Could I + base verbale ? (poli). Exemple : Could I borrow your pen? Can I + base verbale ? (plus familier). Exemple : Can I go out with my friends? Réponse positive : Yes, of course. / Yes, you may. / Sure, go ahead. Réponse négative : I'm afraid not. / No, you may not. / I'd rather you didn't.

1) May I use your phone, please? - Yes, of course, go ahead. 2) Could I stay up a bit later tonight? - I'm afraid not, you have school tomorrow. 3) Can I invite my friends over this weekend? - Yes, you can, but please tidy up afterwards. 4) May I be excused from the table? - Yes, you may.

blocs.enonce: Transforme ces situations en demandes de permission polies avec 'May I' ou 'Could I' : 1) Tu veux emprunter la voiture de ton père. 2) Tu veux regarder la télévision avant de faire tes devoirs. 3) Tu veux sortir avec tes amis ce soir. 4) Tu veux utiliser l'ordinateur de ta sœur.
blocs.solution: 1) May I borrow your car, Dad? / Could I borrow your car, Dad? 2) May I watch television before doing my homework? 3) Could I go out with my friends tonight? 4) May I use your computer, please?

blocs.texte: Pour donner ou refuser une permission, on utilise 'can/may' (autoriser) et 'can't/may not/must not' (interdire).

Donner la permission : You may/can + base verbale. Exemple : You may watch TV for one hour. Refuser/interdire : You can't/may not/must not + base verbale. Exemple : You must not go out after 8 pm. 'Must not' est plus fort et exprime une interdiction stricte, souvent liée à une règle importante.

blocs.titre: Dialogue entre Tim et sa mère
blocs.texte: Tim: Mom, may I go to Jack's house this afternoon? Mom: Have you finished your homework? Tim: Not yet, but I'll finish it tonight. Mom: Then no, you can't go now. You must finish your homework first. Tim: Okay... Can I go after dinner then? Mom: Yes, you may, but you must be back before 9 pm. Tim: Thanks, Mom! Mom: And remember, you must not come back late, it's a school night.

blocs.enonce: D'après le dialogue entre Tim et sa mère, réponds par Vrai ou Faux : 1) Tim has already finished his homework. 2) His mother allows him to go to Jack's house immediately. 3) Tim can go to Jack's house after dinner. 4) Tim must be back before 9 pm.
blocs.solution: 1) Faux (il n'a pas encore fini). 2) Faux (elle refuse d'abord). 3) Vrai. 4) Vrai.

blocs.texte: Les conflits entre parents et enfants sont inévitables (inevitable) dans toutes les familles. Ils surviennent souvent à cause de désaccords sur les limites (boundaries), comme les horaires de sortie, l'utilisation du téléphone, ou les tâches ménagères.

Les principales causes de conflits parent-enfant incluent : les différences d'opinion sur l'indépendance, les règles à la maison, le temps passé sur les écrans, les résultats scolaires, et le choix des amis. Ces conflits peuvent être intenses (intense) mais se résolvent souvent par le dialogue et le compromis (compromise).

Many teenagers feel that their parents don't understand them, while parents often feel their children don't respect the rules. For example, a conflict can start when a teenager wants to stay out late with friends, but the parents are worried about safety. Instead of shouting, both sides can try to find a compromise: the teenager agrees to come home a bit earlier, and the parents agree to extend the curfew slightly.

blocs.enonce: Lis la situation suivante et propose un compromis raisonnable : 'A teenager wants to spend 4 hours a day on his phone after school. His parents think this is too much and want to forbid phone use completely after school.'
blocs.solution: Réponse modèle : A reasonable compromise could be: the teenager is allowed to use his phone for 1 hour after finishing his homework, instead of 4 hours or none at all. Both the teenager's need for relaxation and the parents' concern about study time are respected.
